filename: Reliance on fossil fuels increases during extreme temperature events in the continental United States.pdf
title: Reliance on fossil fuels increases during extreme temperature events in the continental United States
processes: power grid electricity generation response to climate extremes
energy demand and renewable energy generation under extreme heat and cold
code_availability: The python code used to create the figures is available upon request from the corresponding author and will also be further accessed through Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10161493.
testbed_rationale: The study conducts statistical and empirical data analysis of energy system sensitivity to climate extremes. It does not train, evaluate, or benchmark ML models or physics parameterizations.
pain_points: Limitation of available electricity transmission data within the grid to assess mitigation effects of inter-regional electricity transfer during extreme events
Missing cooling demand analysis points in colder states due to threshold limitations
extraction_notes: The paper does not develop or apply machine learning techniques; it uses statistical analysis (bootstrap sampling, linear regression, percentile thresholding) to assess energy and carbon intensity dynamics during temperature extremes.
